page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-360-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine instance from the c3d family, featuring 360 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 180 physical AMD EPYC 9B14 cores. The architecture is x86_64, utilizing SMT with 2.0 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 1440.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. For local storage, it includes 32 NVMe SSDs totaling 12864 GB of bundled local capacity. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across multiple domains. Multi-core CPU performance is in the top 10% with a stress-ng score of 554627.01 and a Passmark CPU score of 157183.11. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 27237.65 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 701.37 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, both placing in the top 10%. Single-core performance is strong, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2021.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3068.37. The instance demonstrates top-tier capabilities in cryptographic operations, database operations, and software compilation, though single-threaded gzip compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the average tier.

With 12864 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and top-tier database operation benchmarks, such as a Passmark database score of 33804.94 and Redis SET performance of 398.84 million operations per second, this instance is configured for large-scale database systems, static web serving, and data-intensive processing. The high resource density of 360 vCPUs and 1440.0 GB RAM offers qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads, such as software compilation and ray tracing, which both score in the top 10%. However, for text generation tasks in large language models, performance drops to average levels, suggesting that GPU-accelerated instances may be more cost-effective for generative AI text generation despite the high CPU core count.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-360-lssd is a general-purpose instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 x86_64 processor, delivering 360 dedicated vCPUs across 180 physical cores and 1440.0 GB of RAM. It features 12864 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across 32 drives. Benchmarks show top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with a Passmark CPU score of 157183.11, and exceptional memory bandwidth of 701.37 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. While single-core performance is strong, multi-threaded execution excels, particularly in software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations, where Redis SET throughput reaches 398.84 million operations per second. This instance is suited for large-scale database hosting, static web serving, and parallelized compute tasks, though its average text-generation speeds for large language models indicate a tradeoff compared to GPU-accelerated alternatives.
